# Numerical solvers {#sec-ch10}

The schemes of the other chapters reduce, at their core, to a few numerical tasks. They solve a small dense
linear system, solve a least-squares problem under linear constraints, take a Newton step that must respect bounds,
interpolate a table, or solve a large sparse system. This chapter describes the kernels in `src/math` that do these
tasks. The dense kernels are written for one small system per thread, on raw row-major arrays, so the same template
runs in a CPU loop and inside a CUDA kernel (@sec-ch12). The interpolation and sparse kernels work on whole `torch`
tensors.

The dependency map of the schemes (a figure) is not drawn yet. In words: the least-squares solvers and the Newton step
are built on the LU kernels; the pseudo-inverse solve is the fallback of the pivoted Gaussian solve in the implicit
kinetics step of @sec-ch06; interpolation and the sparse solver stand alone.

| scheme | entry point | default | main test |
|---|---|---|---|
| @sec-ch10-dense | `dsolve_lu` | always | `test_thermo` (indirect) |
| @sec-ch10-lu | `ludcmp`, `lubksb` | always | `test_thermo` (indirect) |
| @sec-ch10-kkt | `leastsq_kkt` | `reg`[^rg-95aa86ee8f56] 0 | `test_thermo`, `test_alloc_space` |
| @sec-ch10-newton | `constrained_newton_step` | `reg` 0 | `test_thermo` |
| @sec-ch10-pseudo-inverse | `psolve` | always | missing evidence |
| @sec-ch10-interpolation | `interpn` | no extrapolation | missing evidence |
| @sec-ch10-sparse | `cuda_csr_solve_cusolver` | `tol`[^rg-a8da237dabba] 0, `reorder` 0 | `test_atm2d.py` |
